claim: More oxytocin (OT) neurons in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) were activated during pup caring than infanticide in virgin mandarin voles.
source: Here, using monogamous mandarin voles (Microtus mandarinus), we found that more oxytocin (OT) neurons in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) were activated during pup caring than infanticide.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data showing c-Fos expression in OT neurons during different behaviors, as presented in Figure 1.

claim: Optogenetic activation of OT neurons in the PVN facilitated pup caring in male and female mandarin voles.
source: Optogenetic activation of OT neurons in the PVN facilitated pup caring in male and female mandarin voles.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic manipulation experiments showing behavioral changes upon activation of PVN OT neurons, as shown in Figure 2.

claim: In infanticide voles, optogenetic activation of PVN OT cells prolonged latency to approach and attack pups.
source: In infanticide voles, optogenetic activation of PVN OT cells or PVN-medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) OT projection fibers prolonged latency to approach and attack pups, whereas inhibition of these OT neurons or projections facilitated approach and infanticide.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic activation experiments in infanticide voles showing increased latencies to approach and attack pups, as presented in Figure 2.

claim: Inhibition of PVN OT neurons or projections facilitated approach and infanticide in infanticide voles.
source: In infanticide voles, optogenetic activation of PVN OT cells or PVN-medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) OT projection fibers prolonged latency to approach and attack pups, whereas inhibition of these OT neurons or projections facilitated approach and infanticide.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic inhibition experiments showing decreased latencies to approach and attack pups, as presented in Figure 3 and Figure 7.

claim: Optogenetic activation of PVN OT neuron projections to the mPFC in males shortened the latency to approach and retrieve pups and facilitated the initiation of pup care.
source: Optogenetic activation of PVN OT neuron projections to the mPFC in males shortened the latency to approach and retrieve pups and facilitated the initiation of pup care, but produced no effects on pup-care females.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic manipulation of PVN-mPFC projections showing behavioral changes in males, as presented in Figure 6.

claim: Optogenetic activation of PVN OT neuron projections to the mPFC produced no effects on pup-care females.
source: Optogenetic activation of PVN OT neuron projections to the mPFC in males shortened the latency to approach and retrieve pups and facilitated the initiation of pup care, but produced no effects on pup-care females.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic manipulation experiments showing no significant behavioral changes in pup-care females, as presented in Figure 6.

claim: OT release in the mPFC increased upon approaching and retrieving pups in pup-care voles.

claim: OT release in the mPFC decreased upon attacking pups in infanticide voles.

claim: Intraperitoneal injection of OT promoted pup care and inhibited infanticide behavior.
